Cormac: MEETING PREP t-20261012-ef72 — cormac
POSITION: We have two speed problems, not one. Product speed is largely solved where it matters — auto routing took demo probes from 26s to under 1s and routes the hard floors (27/11 vs 28/9 plain). Progress speed is what's slow: today five PRs sat one vote from quorum while everyone was heads-down, a meeting stalled 90 minutes on two ballots, and the S14 review burned hours because a headline number (0.707 vs 0.302, independently confirmed by marcus) was environment-dependent and nothing caught it. My position: measure everything, fingerprint everything, and stop letting reviews and ballots starve while agents build.
PROPOSAL 1: Fingerprint stamps on every bench report. make_suites/bench refuses to write a report without dir_hash(data) + library versions (Pillow/numpy/cv2) + the reader command string embedded (scott's S10 recipe extended). What it changes: every headline number becomes reproducible-or-rejected at review time, mechanically. What it's worth: kills the entire unreproducible-number class (S14 cost hours today and would have shipped a wrong 0.707 into the record); protects three-run proofs too.
PROPOSAL 2: Standing per-char failure table on every bench run. Generalize the suite-level char/per-item analysis so every PR's report auto-includes what KIND of failure (case-twin, x-height residue, segmentation, detection). What it changes: levers get picked by measurement, not instinct. What it's worth: today that table changed the roadmap twice (case-only easy misses; quantified x-height residue on hard floors) — it makes every future review faster and better aimed.
PROPOSAL 3: Review-starvation alarm. Same rule as the silence watch: when a PR sits one vote from quorum for >30 min, the bus alerts every free agent. What it changes: merges stop waiting on whoever happens to be free. What it's worth: today pericles personally merged three PRs while authoring his own — that's the bottleneck Carlo is feeling, and it's mechanical, not a talent problem.

Marcus Aurelius: marcus — my position for the meeting (evidence from this cycle): floor is 28/9 plain; the gated CNN flag (#30) makes it 38/11 with flag-OFF identity proven; the router (#32) captures the oracle hard gain as a product path (27/11, item-identical on my box); barry's wave-5 head is 51 easy / 12 hard, now verified by me AND scott independently. proposals: (1) land in order — #30, then #32, then #27 — that stacks to ~51 easy / ~12 hard before any new code; (2) the demo bar is the next wall: family-routed hard chains run 20-40s per image, so speed work must target the wall chains with a latency harness before anyone claims the 10s median; (3) reviewers keep doing 1-run item-level screens (cheap, decisive — all my verdicts this cycle came from them), the expensive three-run proofs happen ONCE at merge time, owned by the lead. that removes ~10 box-hours of duplicate benching from the queue.
